subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-facing cadence guardrail, with unset/0 preserving current behavior and configured values rejecting or pacing fast recurring jobs?
rationale: The implementation is opt-in, but it adds a new core config surface and deliberate configured fail-closed behavior for recurring schedules, which is a maintainer product and compatibility decision rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Docs Fix
options.body: Keep the new core config surface, refresh `docs/docs_map.md`, rerun exact-head checks, and merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.

options.title: Narrow To Advisory Warnings
options.body: Reject enforcement for now and pursue warning-only high-frequency schedule guidance instead of configured schedule rejection and runtime pacing.

options.title: Defer Core Config Surface
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers choose a broader cron guardrail policy or a less config-heavy operator control.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Docs Fix
recommendation.body: Keep the new core config surface, refresh `docs/docs_map.md`, rerun exact-head checks, and merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.
